summary: Jefferson County DNR live-in tower built 1961 near Kalaloch; staffed 1961-66; spotted a 1967 fire; destroyed 1969; footings remain, reached only by permit.

facts.design: 40' wooden tower with a DNR live-in cab
facts.status_note: Destroyed in 1969; Willhite's trip report describes two footings and an old structure at the summit

staffing.status: first keeper Janice McDowell in 1961; keepers named for 1962, 1963 and 1964-1966

access.note: Private timber company owns the land; Willhite says a permit is required to hike to the site, and permits are sold but not cheap

events.note: 40-foot wooden tower with DNR live-in cab, built by the DNR carpentry crew
Janice McDowell, shifted from a Quinault Indian Reservation lookout (Daily Chronicle, July 1961; Willhite)
Mildred Drazkowski (Willhite); Willhite also has her taking the station later in the 1961 season, moved over from Skidder Hill
Raft River fire, July 1967: lookout ten miles north spotted the smoke; about 6,000 acres by Tuesday morning (The Oregonian, as quoted by Forest Lookouts)
Destroyed in 1969 (register, which also lists it as removed that year; Willhite)
Registered February 11, 2020, nominated by Tammy McLeod

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives 1,963 ft (598 m); Willhite gives 1,018 feet. The brief keeps the register's 598.3 m. No elevation appears in the story, and the two figures are not reconciled.

notes_for_editor: Jefferson County site only. Do not merge with the Clearwater lookout in Garfield County (Umatilla NF, 82-foot steel tower that firelookout.com describes as available for emergencies) or with the Clearwater South emergency site near the 705 ft benchmark, which Willhite describes separately. Willhite's trip report is undated, so the footings and permit details are as of an unknown visit. The 1942-44 Air Warning Service station 'Baker 4-4' listed on the Forest Lookouts page is not in the story because the sources do not say it stood on this lookout site. The register's 'Removed' field and the brief's 'removed' event are the same year as 'destroyed'; the record uses 'destroyed'.
